METAPET.SCHOOL

The classroom edition is free, and that is the whole model.

MetaPet School is a teacher-led classroom product for Years 3-6. Seven short sessions, run on the school's own devices, with an alias-only roster and no student accounts to create, manage or delete at the end of term.

There is no licence, no per-student price and no paid tier. Not a trial, not a freemium tier, not a pilot rate that changes later. The complete experience — every session, the printable fallback, the teacher pack and the full governance pack — is A$0 for every school, permanently.

It gets its own domain because a classroom product should not have to explain which parts of a consumer site a ten-year-old is allowed to touch. The boundary is enforced in the routing layer, not in a policy document.

This does not replace the software that runs your school

Keep your existing school platform for attendance, payments, timetables and communication. MetaPet School performs a different job: it gives children a bounded learning experience without requiring another student identity system.

It is not a school-management system, a learning management system, a parent portal or a behaviour-points platform.

What happens to the data?

No student account, student email, real name, photo or login is required by the classroom build. Classroom record contents stay in this browser on this device during routine use. The supervising adult can delete the covered classroom records immediately from the local-data controls or by clearing this site's browser data.

Teacher-chosen aliases, lesson progress, classroom setup choices, class summary counts and any light evidence a teacher records.
Where is it stored?
Classroom record contents stay in this browser on this device during routine use. Routine classroom use does not sync those record contents to B$S.
Why is it needed?
So a class can pause and resume a session, and so a teacher can review light evidence without re-running the lesson.
Who can see it?
Anyone using this browser profile on this device. That is why it belongs on a teacher-controlled device or browser profile.
When does it disappear?
After 35 days without use, expired classroom records are removed when a school route next opens; a website cannot erase browser storage while it is closed.
How does a teacher delete it?
From the local-data controls, with an explicit confirmation. No deletion request to the studio is needed.
What is never required?
No student account, student email, real name, photo or login is required by the classroom build.

After 35 days without use, inactive records are cleared when a school route next opens. This does not replace the software that runs your school

Keep your existing school platform for attendance, payments, timetables and communication. MetaPet School performs a different job: it gives children a bounded learning experience without requiring another student identity system.

It is not a school-management system, a learning management system, a parent portal or a behaviour-points platform.

What children do

Seven sessions, about 15–20 minutes each. Each one gives a class one instruction at a time, one reflection question, and a visible stopping point.

1
Meet the System
Watch the companion, give it one input, and say what changed.
2
Read the Signals
Look at the companion's signals, name one, and choose a settling action.
3
One Identity, Many Representations
Compare two views of the same companion and find what stayed the same.
4
Choices and Algorithms
Predict what one action will do, try it, then reset and try a different order.
5
Privacy and Responsible Design
Sort what a system should keep, should ask about, and should never keep.
6
Design a Better Feature
Change one part of the design and say who your change helps.
7
Test, Reflect and Improve
Test one idea, find a pattern from earlier sessions, and explain it.
What teachers do

Open the lesson. Guide the activity. Capture light evidence. Get back to teaching.

What you need
Years 3-6 class
About 20 minutes
A teacher to lead it
A browser - nothing to install
No student accounts to create
A printer if you want the paper fallback
One class is enough to start

Field Mode caches its pages so a session can survive a dropped connection mid-lesson, and every session has a printable fallback. Full offline operation has not been verified across school hardware yet.

What happens to the data?

No student account, student email, real name, photo or login is required by the classroom build. Classroom record contents stay in this browser on this device during routine use. The supervising adult can delete the covered classroom records immediately from the local-data controls or by clearing this site's browser data.

What is stored?
Teacher-chosen aliases, lesson progress, classroom setup choices, class summary counts and any light evidence a teacher records.
Where is it stored?
Classroom record contents stay in this browser on this device during routine use. Routine classroom use does not sync those record contents to B$S.
Why is it needed?
So a class can pause and resume a session, and so a teacher can review light evidence without re-running the lesson.
Who can see it?
Anyone using this browser profile on this device. That is why it belongs on a teacher-controlled device or browser profile.
When does it disappear?
After 35 days without use, expired classroom records are removed when a school route next opens; a website cannot erase browser storage while it is closed.
How does a teacher delete it?
From the local-data controls, with an explicit confirmation. No deletion request to the studio is needed.
What is never required?
No student account, student email, real name, photo or login is required by the classroom build.

After 35 days without use, inactive records are cleared when a school route next opens. We are not claiming there is no data, no risk, or blanket regulatory compliance — the accurate statement is narrower: routine classroom use does not submit classroom-record contents to B$S, the host still receives ordinary page requests, and deletion is in a supervising adult's hands.
